I farm a small wheat-maize rotation field, and with 7.8 mu and only two people in the household, I will keep the whole 7.8 mu in the usual pattern: winter wheat first, then summer maize on the same land. I have farmed here for 40 years, so I do what is steady and manageable, not anything complicated. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on stable water at the key stages instead of gambling on rainfall. For wheat, I will use improved seed, give enough nitrogen for steady tillering and grain filling, and add phosphorus and potassium as base fertilizer because the land has already been cropped for many years. I will use rotary tillage because it saves labor and suits my scale. I will spray a limited number of times, mainly only when weeds or disease pressure show up, because I want to control cost. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid maize on the same 7.8 mu because hybrid maize gives me more stable yield. For maize, I will keep fertilizer a bit heavier on nitrogen, irrigate at key stages if rain is short, and do fewer pesticide applications unless pressure becomes obvious. My goal this year is not to chase the highest possible output, but to secure a reliable harvest with inputs I can manage myself.
